title: Hereditarily small sets: hereditary cardinality

based_on.title: An Introduction to Set Theory
based_on.pages: 101–102 (Theorem 41, Exercise 34, and the finite case of Theorem 42)

summary: Hereditary size bounds membership rank and defines transitive sets closed under suitably small set formation.
abstract: A set with few members can still contain a very large set. Hereditary size counts everything reached by following membership repeatedly, including the starting set. Bounding this size gives a transitive collection of sets with bounded membership rank. At the first uncountable bound, these are the sets with countably many membership descendants; they include every subset of the natural numbers but exclude the set of all such subsets. When the bound is regular, collecting fewer than that many hereditarily small sets produces another hereditarily small set. A singular bound can fail this closure even for a countable collection.
